root_cause.text: A race condition exists because the asynchronous partition scan work (ublk_partition_scan_work) accesses ub->ub_disk without holding a reference, while the device teardown path in ublk_stop_dev detaches and may free the disk, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail: "1. ublk_ctrl_start_dev() schedules partition_scan_work after add_disk() 2. ublk_stop_dev() calls ublk_stop_dev_unlocked() which does: del_gendisk(ub->ub_disk), ublk_detach_disk() sets ub->ub_disk = NULL, put_disk() which may free the disk 3. The worker ublk_partition_scan_work() then dereferences ub->ub_disk leading to UAF". The patch fixes this by using ublk_get_disk()/ublk_put_disk() in the worker to hold a reference and by changing flush_work() to cancel_work_sync().

Author: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Dec 23 11:27:40 2025 +0800

    ublk: scan partition in async way
    
    Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
    tables. Similar to nvme_partition_scan_work(), partition scanning is
    deferred to a work queue to prevent deadlocks.
    
    When partition scan happens synchronously during add_disk(), IO errors
    can cause the partition scan to wait while hold
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces `ublk_partition_scan_work` which accesses `ub->ub_disk` without taking a reference (lines 258-269). The work is scheduled in `ublk_ctrl_start_dev` after `add_disk()` (line 3000-3001). In `ublk_stop_dev`, the call to `flush_work` happens after `ublk_stop_dev_unlocked` (which likely detaches the disk) and after releasing `ub->mutex` (line 2044-2046). This ordering means the work can run after the disk has been detached/freed, leading to a use-after-free. No protection (such as a disk reference or ordering fix) is present.
